tools.name: get_audio_features
tools.description:
Get audio features for ONE track — BPM, musical key (name + Camelot + Open Key),
    energy, danceability, valence, acousticness, loudness, mood, mood_vector, genre, time signature, duration and more.
    `preview_loudness.integrated_lufs` is the BS.1770 integrated loudness (LUFS) of the 30-second
    preview — often the chorus, so typically a little louder than the full track.

    Fields follow the layout of Spotify's retired /audio-features endpoint.
    Provide AT LEAST ONE identifier — if you know several, send them all rather than
    choosing; they resolve by precedence (`track` > `isrc` > `mbid` > `spotify_id`) and
    the rest are ignored:
      - `track` (optionally with `artist`) — e.g. track="Blinding Lights", artist="The Weeknd".
      - `isrc` — e.g. "USUM71900001".
      - `mbid` — a MusicBrainz recording UUID.
      - `spotify_id` — a Spotify track ID, URI, or URL (resolved per request by reading
        the track's title from Spotify's public embed page and matching it against our
        catalogue — no Spotify IDs are stored; ambiguous titles miss rather than guess —
        prefer `track`/`isrc` for full coverage).

    Returns a JSON object of features. Some feature fields may be null for tracks resolved
    via the fallback catalogs (only audio-derived values are present for fully analysed
    tracks).

    VALUES are FreqBlog's own analysis, NOT on Spotify's scale: energy and valence are
    models of how energetic / positive the preview sounds, both on our own scales (derive thresholds from our values, don't copy Spotify-tuned ones);
    danceability and acousticness are on AcousticBrainz's scale -- its classifier where
    available, else a model that listens to the preview, built on PANNs embeddings
    (Kong et al. 2020, CC BY 4.0); instrumentalness is a vocal-detection model's score for
    the 30-second preview (not the whole track); speechiness and liveness are currently
    null for catalogue tracks; time_signature is ASSUMED 4 (4/4) on every track, not
    measured. KEY: treat `key` as a best guess when `key_confidence` < 0.8 (measured against
    musicians' annotations: at >= 0.9 it is exact 77% / Camelot-compatible 88%).

    If a track name is not yet in the catalog, the API holds the request during the
    on-demand ingest and usually returns the fully analysed track inline in this same call;
    only if the ingest runs long does it fall back to a queued response you can re-poll
    shortly (~15s). If the track turns out not to be on any streaming source we can analyse,
    you get a definitive not-found instead — that verdict is terminal for ~7 days, so don't
    retry it. If you only have a fuzzy or partial name, call search_catalog first to
    find the exact track.

track.description: Track title. Use with `artist` when known. Supply AT LEAST ONE of track/isrc/mbid/spotify_id. Sending several is fine — they resolve by precedence (track > isrc > mbid > spotify_id) and the rest are ignored.
track.title: Track

artist.description: Artist name. Only used with `track`; required when the title is <=2 characters.
artist.title: Artist

mbid.description: MusicBrainz recording ID (UUID). The precise key when there is no ISRC, e.g. pre-1986 recordings.
mbid.title: Mbid

spotify_id.description: Spotify track ID, 'spotify:track:...' URI, or open.spotify.com URL. Resolved per request by reading the track's title from Spotify's public embed page and matching it against our catalogue (no Spotify IDs are stored) — a title several artists share is ambiguous and misses rather than guessing; prefer track (+artist) or isrc.
spotify_id.title: Spotify Id

tools.name: get_audio_features_batch
tools.description:
Get audio features for MANY tracks in one call (up to 50 processed) — ideal for
    analysing a whole playlist at once. Identify each item by name (`track`/`artist`), by
    `isrc` (matched exactly first — best for CJK / K-pop / niche tracks whose fuzzy
    name-match misses), or both (ISRC first, name as the fallback).

    One bad entry never fails the batch. Items beyond the 50-per-call cap come back with
    `found: false` and `backfill_status: "over_limit"`; an item missing BOTH `track` and
    `isrc` comes back `"invalid_no_query"`. Neither is processed or charged — the response's
    `skipped` field counts them, so split a long list into calls of <=50 and resubmit any
    skipped rows.

    Returns counts (`found` / `not_found` / `skipped`) plus a per-track `results` array, where
    each entry's `result` is the same feature object as get_audio_features (or null when not
    found), and `isrc` is echoed back. An item is billed only when it returns features or
    queues an on-demand ingest; an ISRC/name with no match anywhere is free. A track you
    queue and then collect costs ONE unit, not two — the call that collects it is free.
    For a `found: false` item, `backfill_status` `queued` / `processing` / `deferred` means
    retry later; `unavailable` is terminal (carries `terminal`, `reason`, `retry_after_days` —
    treat it as a miss until then); null means no match anywhere.
    For a single track, use get_audio_features.
    On this shared connector each caller can process up to 500 tracks a day through this tool (resets 00:00 UTC); rows past that come back `found: false` with `backfill_status: "daily_cap"`.

TrackQuery.description:
One track to look up by name and/or ISRC. Supply `track` or `isrc` (or both); an item
carrying neither is skipped by the batch tool (`invalid_no_query`), not an error.

track.description: Track title. Supply this OR `isrc` (or both — ISRC is matched exactly first, the name is the fallback).
track.title: Track

isrc.description: ISRC, e.g. 'USUM71900001' (hyphens optional). Matched exactly first — resolves CJK/K-pop/niche tracks whose fuzzy name-match misses. Supply this OR `track`.
isrc.title: Isrc

TrackQuery.title: TrackQuery

tracks.description: List of {track?, artist?, isrc?} objects. Up to 50 are processed per call; any extra (up to 200 accepted) come back skipped. Each item should carry `track` or `isrc`.
tracks.title: Tracks

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description:
Full-text search the catalog by any mix of track / artist / album tokens. Use this to
    resolve a fuzzy, partial, or misspelled name into concrete tracks BEFORE calling
    get_audio_features.

    Each hit carries `chart_peak`: the best chart position we hold, 1-100 with 100 = a
    number-one. `null` means no placement we hold — treat that as UNKNOWN, not unpopular,
    and note it is NOT an audience-size figure. Placements come from the Apple Music and
    Deezer charts we track (since Aug 2026) and Billboard year-end charts (1960-2025).

    Returns lightweight stubs (itunes_track_id, track_name, artist_name, album, etc.) ranked
    by relevance — NOT audio features. Take the best match's track_name + artist_name and
    pass them to get_audio_features, or reuse its itunes_track_id as a `track_id` seed for
    discovery tools.

    ⚠ Each hit carries a `seedable` boolean. Only a hit with `seedable: true` can be used as
    a seed for get_recommendations / suggest_next_track / build_setlist / score_transition —
    those work off the similarity index, which holds only tracks we have analysed, and about
    a quarter of the catalogue is not analysed yet. **Prefer the highest-ranked hit with
    `seedable: true`.** Seeding with a `seedable: false` id returns a 404; if that track is
    the one you want, call get_audio_features on it first to queue analysis, then retry.

q.description: Search query — any mix of artist / track / album tokens.
q.title: Q

tools.name: find_tracks_by_bpm
tools.description:
Find catalog tracks near a target tempo. Returns tracks whose BPM is within
    +/-`tolerance` of `bpm`, ordered by closeness then by an internal catalogue ordering key (not an audience metric) — useful for DJ set
    planning, workout playlists, or tempo-matching. Each returned track carries full audio
    features. To also constrain by musical key, combine with find_tracks_by_key.

tools.name: find_tracks_by_key
tools.description:
Find catalog tracks in a given musical key — for harmonic mixing and key-locked
    playlists. `key` accepts Camelot ("8A"), Open Key ("1m"), or a key name ("A-Minor",
    "F#-Major"). Returns tracks ordered by an internal catalogue ordering key (not an audience metric), each with full audio features. To
    discover which keys mix well with a given key first, use find_compatible_keys.

key.description: Camelot ('8A'), Open Key ('1m'), or key name ('A-Minor', 'F#-Major').
key.title: Key

tools.name: discover_tracks
tools.description:
Find catalog tracks by criteria, with no seed track: tempo, key, genre, release year,
    chart placement and audio-feature ranges in one call — e.g. house at 122-126 BPM in 8A or
    its neighbours with energy above 0.7: min={"tempo": 122, "energy": 0.7},
    max={"tempo": 126}, key="8A", harmonic=true, genre="house".

    At least one narrowing filter is required (a tempo/feature bound, key, mode, genre, year
    or chart). Returns `results` (one per recording, each with its bpm, camelot, energy,
    danceability, valence, acousticness and loudness_db plus catalog metadata),
    `total_matches` (exact up to 1,000; `total_matches_capped` above that), `next_offset`
    for the next page, and `filters` — what was applied and how many tracks each filter
    removed (`dropped_by`); if the list is short, loosen the largest one. energy, danceability
    and valence are on FreqBlog's own scales, so derive thresholds from values you have seen
    rather than from another service's. Results reach a depth of 500 per query; narrow the
    filters to go further. Pass a result's itunes_track_id to get_audio_features for every
    field, or to suggest_next_track / build_setlist. Costs 1 quota unit.

min.description: HARD lower bounds, e.g. {'tempo': 122, 'energy': 0.7}. Tracks below the bound, and tracks with no analysed value, are excluded. Attributes: acousticness, danceability, duration_ms, energy, loudness, tempo, valence.
min.title: Min

max.description: HARD upper bounds, e.g. {'tempo': 126}. Same attributes as `min`; combine the two for a range.
max.title: Max

target.description: PREFERRED values, e.g. {'energy': 0.8}: nearest first, nothing removed. Same attributes as `min`.
target.title: Target

tempo_match.description: 'exact' (default) or 'half_double' — also match double/half the min/max tempo range (an 87 BPM track for a 174 BPM set).
tempo_match.title: Tempo Match

key.description: Comma list of keys: Camelot ('8A'), Open Key ('1m') or names ('A minor').
key.title: Key

harmonic.description: Widen each key to its harmonically compatible keys (same, relative, one step either way on the Camelot wheel).
harmonic.title: Harmonic

genre.description: Comma list of catalog genre names, e.g. 'house' or 'hip-hop,r&b'. Unknown names in a list are skipped and listed in filters.ignored with close matches; only a list where every name is unknown is rejected.
genre.title: Genre

include_subgenres.description: Also match every subgenre of a top-level genre.
include_subgenres.title: Include Subgenres

explicit.description: true = explicit tracks only, false = non-explicit only; omit for either.
explicit.title: Explicit

charted.description: true = only tracks with a known chart placement (about 4% of tracks have one).
charted.title: Charted

min_chart_peak.description: Best chart position required, as chart_peak (1-100, 100 = a number one).
min_chart_peak.title: Min Chart Peak

sort.description: 'chart' (default: charted first, then newest), 'newest', 'oldest', 'tempo', '-tempo', 'energy', '-energy', or 'target' (default when `target` is given).
sort.title: Sort

offset.description: Skip this many tracks for the next page; offset + limit may not exceed 500.
offset.title: Offset

tools.name: find_similar_tracks
tools.description:
Tracks that SOUND like one seed track or a set of up to 10, optionally restricted by
    tempo, key, genre, year, chart or audio-feature ranges — e.g. "like these three, but
    120-128 BPM in 8A or its neighbours": seed_tracks=[...], min={"tempo": 120},
    max={"tempo": 128}, key="8A", harmonic=true.

    Ranked mainly on a PANNs audio embedding (how the recording sounds) blended with an
    audio-feature similarity. Results are one per recording, with `score`, `genre_relation`
    to the seed and, with several seeds, `matched_seed`. With filters, results are the
    closest-sounding tracks that pass every filter, and `filters` reports what was applied
    and how many catalog tracks each one removed (`dropped_by`) — loosen the largest if the
    list is short. Use get_recommendations instead when you want preferred target values
    (target energy etc.) rather than hard filters. Costs 1 quota unit.
    PANNs (Kong et al., 2020) is used under CC BY 4.0.

track_id.description: One seed: a catalog itunes_track_id (from search_catalog or get_audio_features). Omit when using seed_tracks / seed_isrcs.
track_id.title: Track Id

seed_tracks.description: Several seeds: catalog itunes_track_ids (up to 10 together with seed_isrcs).
seed_tracks.title: Seed Tracks

seed_isrcs.description: Several seeds by ISRC (up to 10 together with seed_tracks).
seed_isrcs.title: Seed Isrcs

blend.description: With several seeds: 'all' (default) = sounds like the set as a whole, best when the seeds share a style; 'any' = every seed gets its own neighbours, interleaved — use it when the seeds are from different genres, where 'all' would average them into tracks that sound like none of them.
blend.title: Blend

min.description: Filter — HARD lower bounds on the results, e.g. {'tempo': 120, 'energy': 0.6}. Attributes: acousticness, danceability, duration_ms, energy, loudness, tempo, valence.
min.title: Min

max.description: Filter — HARD upper bounds, e.g. {'tempo': 128}. Same attributes as `min`.
max.title: Max

tempo_match.description: With a tempo bound: 'exact' (default) or 'half_double' (also match double/half the range).
tempo_match.title: Tempo Match

key.description: Filter — comma list of keys: Camelot ('8A'), Open Key ('1m') or names ('A minor').
key.title: Key

harmonic.description: Widen each key to its harmonically compatible keys.
harmonic.title: Harmonic

genre.description: Filter — comma list of catalog genre names, e.g. 'house'. Unknown names in a list are skipped and listed in filters.ignored with close matches; only a list where every name is unknown is rejected.
genre.title: Genre

include_subgenres.description: Also match every subgenre of a top-level genre.
include_subgenres.title: Include Subgenres

explicit.description: Filter — true = explicit only, false = non-explicit only.
explicit.title: Explicit

charted.description: Filter — true = only tracks with a known chart placement.
charted.title: Charted

min_chart_peak.description: Filter — best chart position required, as chart_peak (100 = a number one).
min_chart_peak.title: Min Chart Peak

cross_genre.description: Genre lane: 'auto' (default, keep results mixable with the seed's genre), 'allow' (genre-blind), 'strict' (seed's genre family only).
cross_genre.title: Cross Genre

exclude_same_artist.description: Drop other tracks by the seed artist(s).
exclude_same_artist.title: Exclude Same Artist

tools.name: search_by_description
tools.description:
Find catalog tracks from a plain-language description of how they sound — e.g.
    "melancholic piano, slow", "dark ambient strings", "upbeat acoustic guitar, fast".

    Understands instruments and voice (piano, guitar, acoustic guitar, violin, cello, strings,
    harp, flute, sax, brass, organ, choir, a cappella, rap, 808/drum machine, orchestral),
    mood (sad/melancholic, dark/eerie, angry, ambient, happy/upbeat, chill/relaxed),
    character (acoustic, instrumental, with vocals, energetic, soft, danceable), tempo
    (slow <= 95 BPM, mid-tempo, fast >= 125 BPM, applied as filters) and any catalog genre.
    Sound words are scored from audio analysis of each track, not titles; every word has to
    hold. The response's `description.understood` shows how each word was read and
    `ignored_words` lists words that were NOT used — rephrase those. Each result has `match`
    (0-1) and a per-word `matched` breakdown. Costs 1 quota unit.

q.description: Plain-language description, e.g. 'melancholic piano, slow' or 'chill acoustic guitar'.
q.title: Q

genre.description: Optional: only these catalog genres (comma list), in addition to any genre named in q. Unknown names in a list are skipped and listed in filters.ignored with close matches; only a list where every name is unknown is rejected.
genre.title: Genre

key.description: Optional: only these keys — Camelot ('8A'), Open Key ('1m') or names.
key.title: Key

min.description: Optional HARD lower bounds, e.g. {'tempo': 120}. Attributes: acousticness, danceability, duration_ms, energy, loudness, tempo, valence.
min.title: Min

offset.description: Skip this many tracks for the next page; offset + limit <= 500.
offset.title: Offset

tools.name: find_compatible_keys
tools.description:
Given a Camelot key (e.g. "8A", "12B"), return the harmonically compatible keys for DJ
    mixing — the same key, the relative major/minor, and the adjacent +/-1 keys on the
    Camelot wheel. With `extended=true` also returns the +7/-7 energy-boost / energy-drop
    keys. Pure music theory — no catalog lookup and no quota cost. Pair with find_tracks_by_key
    to then pull actual tracks in each compatible key.

extended.description: Also return the +7/-7 energy-boost / energy-drop keys.
extended.title: Extended

tools.name: score_transition
tools.description:
Score how well one catalog track mixes into another (0-100) — the pairwise DJ transition
    score no raw key/BPM API gives you. Combines Camelot-wheel key compatibility, octave-aware
    BPM proximity (half/double-time counts as a match), and energy smoothness.

    Returns the overall `score`, per-component scores (`harmonic`/`tempo`/`energy`), a `detail`
    block (key_relation, both Camelot keys, both BPMs, bpm_delta, bpm_octave_matched, both
    energies, energy_delta), and a one-line human `reason` (e.g. "8A->9A adjacent (+1), 126->128
    BPM (+2), energy +0.04 — clean uplifting mix"). Both ids are catalog itunes_track_ids — get
    them from search_catalog or the itunes_track_id field of a get_audio_features result. Costs
    1 quota unit.

from_track_id.description: The track you're mixing FROM — a catalog itunes_track_id, e.g. 'apple_ad1829eeccb70f9a'.
from_track_id.title: From Track Id

to_track_id.description: The candidate track you're mixing INTO — a catalog itunes_track_id.
to_track_id.title: To Track Id

tools.name: suggest_next_track
tools.description:
Given a seed track, return the top-N catalog tracks to play NEXT, ranked by transition
    score. Each suggestion carries the same `score`, per-component scores and human `reason` as
    score_transition (e.g. "11B->11B same key, 118->117 BPM (-0.29), energy +0.12"), plus its
    `genre` and `genre_relation` to the seed. GENRE-AWARE by default (cross_genre=auto): off-genre
    picks that only coincidentally share the seed's key/BPM sink to the bottom — use
    cross_genre=strict for same-genre-family only, or allow for the old harmonic-only ranking. It
    is the seed's sonic neighbours re-ranked for a clean mix.

    Returns `seed`, `count`, and a `suggestions` array of {track, score, components, reason}.
    seed_track_id is a catalog itunes_track_id from search_catalog or a get_audio_features
    result. Pair with build_setlist to order a whole crate. Costs 3 quota units.

seed_track_id.description: The track currently playing — a catalog itunes_track_id.
seed_track_id.title: Seed Track Id

n.description: How many next-track suggestions to return (default 10).
n.title: N

min_score.description: Drop candidates below this overall transition score (default 0).
min_score.title: Min Score

exclude_same_artist.description: Drop tracks by the seed's artist (default false).
exclude_same_artist.title: Exclude Same Artist

bpm_drift.description: Max BPM difference pre-filter before scoring (default 12).
bpm_drift.title: Bpm Drift

max_key_distance.description: Max Camelot-wheel hops pre-filter before scoring (default 2).
max_key_distance.title: Max Key Distance

cross_genre.description: Genre handling: 'auto' (default) keeps picks in a mixable genre lane so an off-genre track that only shares key/BPM sinks to the bottom; 'strict' = same genre-family only; 'allow' = genre-blind (harmonic+tempo+energy only).
cross_genre.title: Cross Genre

tools.name: build_setlist
tools.description:
Order a crate of 2-100 catalog tracks into a beat-matched DJ set that follows an energy
    arc, keeping each consecutive transition harmonically and tempo-smooth. `arc` is one of
    peak_time (default — builds to a peak then eases), warmup, cooldown, or flat.

    Returns the `arc`, `count`, an overall `flow_score` (0-100), the `tracks` in play order, the
    per-step `transitions` ({from_index, to_index, score, reason}), and `omitted` (ids not found
    in the catalog, or with no audio features on file yet). Feed tracks[].itunes_track_id into a Rekordbox/Serato export to drop the set
    straight into your DJ software. track_ids are catalog itunes_track_ids. Costs 5 quota units.

track_ids.description: The crate to order — 2 to 100 catalog itunes_track_ids.
track_ids.title: Track Ids

start_track_id.description: Optional fixed opener — must be one of track_ids.
start_track_id.title: Start Track Id

tools.name: get_recommendations
tools.description:
Recommended tracks for one or more seed tracks, in the shape of Spotify's retired
    GET /v1/recommendations. Takes up to 5 catalog seed tracks and returns catalogue tracks that
    sound like the set as a whole — ranked on the same similarity as find_similar_tracks (mainly a
    PANNs audio embedding, blended with audio features), RE-RANKED by genre affinity (so a
    close-sounding cross-genre track doesn't outrank same-genre picks).

    Returns `seeds` (each {id, found}), `count`, and `tracks` (each {track, score,
    genre_relation}; each track carries its `genre`). `genre_relation` is "same", "compatible"
    (different but mixable family), "cross" (unrelated), or "unknown" (either side has no mapped
    genre), measured against the PRIMARY seed — the first of your seed_tracks we could actually
    use, so reordering seed_tracks changes it and a skipped seed never becomes the reference.
    With a SINGLE seed the field is the ranking's own verdict, so it explains the order (same as
    suggest_next_track). With SEVERAL seeds the ranking considers ALL of them while the label stays
    relative to your primary seed, so a "cross" label on a multi-seed call does NOT mean the track
    was pushed down — it may share a family with another of your seeds. `score` is the similarity
    to the seed set (the same blended similarity find_similar_tracks returns); genre affinity and
    target_ preferences influence the ORDER, not the score, so the list is NOT strictly
    score-descending.
    Use cross_genre=strict to return same-genre-family tracks ONLY (off-genre dropped
    server-side), or allow to disable the genre ranking. seed_tracks are catalog itunes_track_ids
    from search_catalog or the itunes_track_id field of a get_audio_features result.

    NO id? Pass `track` (+ optional `artist`) instead and we resolve the name to the best catalog
    match and seed on it — the resolved track is echoed back as `seed_query`; seed_tracks wins if
    both are given.

    TUNING: `min`/`max` are HARD filters and `target` is a preference (nearer ranks higher,
    nothing removed), over acousticness, danceability, duration_ms, energy,
    loudness, tempo and valence. NOTE: `popularity` (2026-08-27), `liveness`, `speechiness`
    (2026-09-26) and `instrumentalness` (2026-09-27) are RETIRED as tunables and return a 400 —
    popularity recorded how a track entered our catalogue, not audience size; the other three
    are returned as null for catalogue tracks. Values are FreqBlog's own (not Spotify's):
    energy and valence (models of how energetic / positive the preview sounds) on our own scales, danceability/acousticness on AcousticBrainz's scale —
    derive thresholds from our values rather than reusing Spotify-tuned ones. e.g. min={"tempo": 100},
    max={"tempo": 130}, target={"energy": 0.8} for energetic 100-130 BPM tracks. When you tune,
    the response adds a `filters` block saying what applied, how many tracks each bound removed
    (`dropped_by`) and whether the bounds ran out of catalogue before `limit` (`limit_reached`)
    — if the list comes back short, read that BEFORE assuming the catalogue is thin.
    Costs 2 quota units.

seed_tracks.description: 1-5 catalog itunes_track_ids to base recommendations on, e.g. ['apple_ad1829eeccb70f9a'] (blended into a feature-space centroid). Omit and use track(+artist) to seed by name instead.
seed_tracks.title: Seed Tracks

track.description: Seed by track NAME instead of an id — resolved to the best catalog match (echoed back as seed_query). Pair with artist to disambiguate. Ignored when seed_tracks is given.
track.title: Track

artist.description: Artist name narrowing the track seed (case-insensitive).
artist.title: Artist

exclude_seed_artists.description: Drop tracks by any of the seed artists (default false).
exclude_seed_artists.title: Exclude Seed Artists

cross_genre.description: Genre handling (mirrors suggest_next_track): 'auto' (default) re-ranks by genre affinity so a feature-close cross-genre track can't outrank same-genre picks; 'strict' = same genre-family only (off-genre dropped server-side); 'allow' = genre-blind (pure audio-feature cosine).
cross_genre.title: Cross Genre

min.description: HARD lower bounds, e.g. {'tempo': 100, 'energy': 0.5}. Tracks below the bound — and tracks we hold no analysed value for — are dropped. Attributes: acousticness, danceability, duration_ms, energy, loudness, tempo, valence.
min.title: Min

max.description: HARD upper bounds, e.g. {'tempo': 130}. Same attributes as `min`. Combine the two for a range.
max.title: Max

target.description: PREFERRED values, e.g. {'energy': 0.8}. Tracks nearer the value rank higher; unlike min/max nothing is removed. Same attributes as `min`.
target.title: Target

tools.name: get_related_artists
tools.description:
Artists related to a seed artist, in the shape of Spotify's retired
    GET /v1/artists/{id}/related-artists. No artist graph exists, so we derive one: build the
    seed artist's track-vector centroid, take its nearest catalogue tracks, aggregate by artist
    (each scored on its top-3 track similarities so a prolific artist can't dominate) plus a
    same-genre lift and a cross-genre penalty.

    Returns `artist`, `count`, and `related` (each {artist_name, score, match_count,
    sample_track_id}). Pass a sample_track_id straight to get_audio_features or
    suggest_next_track. Costs 2 quota units.

artist.description: Seed artist name (as it appears in the catalog; case-insensitive).
artist.title: Artist

limit.description: Number of related artists to return (default 20).
limit.title: Limit

tools.name: tag_track
tools.description:
Get a compact, clearly labelled tag list for a track — energy / danceability / valence /
    acousticness / instrumentalness (instrumental vs vocal, judged on the 30-second
    preview), plus a mood tag and a broad genre tag. It is a tag-shaped
    projection of the same open-data analysis get_audio_features returns (no audio upload, no extra
    compute), so it costs the same 1 quota unit, charged only on a served result.

    EVERY tag carries its own `confidence` and `provenance`:
      - confidence: measured (a numeric audio feature, source in provenance) | derived (MIREX mood from valence+energy) |
        model-estimated (AcousticBrainz mood SVM probability — research-grade, raw prob in `value`) |
        catalog-genre (broad catalogue tag, not fine-grained).
      - provenance: librosa | panns | valence+energy | acousticbrainz | catalog.
    `value` is the [0,1] score for numeric tags and null for label-only tags (mood category, genre).

    Provide AT LEAST ONE identifier: `track` (optionally with `artist`), `isrc`, `mbid`,
    `spotify_id`, or `track_id` (catalog itunes_track_id). If you know several, send them all —
    they resolve by precedence (`track` > `isrc` > `track_id` > `mbid` > `spotify_id`) and the
    rest are ignored, so you never have to pick. The broad, reliable coverage is the
    MEASURED tags from our own analysis (librosa + a PANNs-based model) over the analysed catalogue
    (plus on-demand by name);
    MBID/ISRC additionally reach 7.5M+ AcousticBrainz recordings WHEN you supply that identifier.

    Returns { track, count, tags:[{tag, category, value, confidence, provenance}], disclaimer }.
    For the full numeric feature set use get_audio_features; for nearest tracks use a discovery tool.

track.description: Track title. Use with `artist` when known. Supply AT LEAST ONE of track/isrc/mbid/spotify_id/track_id. Sending several is fine — they resolve by precedence (track > isrc > track_id > mbid > spotify_id).
